steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The NEA (Non-Exam Assessment) is a practical project that typically contributes 25-40% of the GCSE grade.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: AQA Engineering NEA (40%): students produce engineering drawings, a working prototype and a portfolio.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: WJEC Eduqas has two NEA units: Manufacturing Engineering Products (Unit 1) and Designing Engineering Products (Unit 2).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The portfolio must show clear progression through research, design, planning, manufacture and evaluation stages.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Describe the structure of a strong NEA portfolio. | Q: Why is annotation important in the NEA portfolio? | Q: Explain how to evaluate the finished NEA product against the specification.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 1) Context and brief. 2) Research: existing products, materials, processes. 3) Specification: measurable criteria. 4) Design development: initial ideas to final design. 5) Manufacturing plan: operatio | Annotation explains the reasoning behind design decisions. Without annotation, the examiner cannot understand why decisions were made. Good annotation links each decision to a specification requiremen | Take each specification criterion in turn and test whether the product meets it. Record results with photographic evidence. If any criterion is not met, explain why and suggest improvements.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: In NEA questions, emphasise the LINK between stages: research informs specification, which drives design, which guides manufacture, which is evaluated against the specification. Annotation is the most commonly under-used NEA skill - annotate everything. Evaluation must reference specific specification criteria - generic comments gain no marks. Show design DEVELOPMENT: initial ideas should differ from the final design, with clear reasons for changes. Manufacturing plans must be realistic and specific - name actual tools, machines and materials.
